activity.notes: Cunhambebe was the pre-eminent Tupinambá/Tamoio leader in the indigenous confederation fighting Portuguese expansion on the São Paulo–Rio de Janeiro coast. Sources warn that the name may refer to a father and son; this record represents the senior Cunhambebe described as the confederation's leading chief and dying around 1555. ATLAS uses the actual Tamoyo Confederation rather than the broad ethnolinguistic label Tupi.

sources.title: O Rio dos Navegantes — Museu de Arte do Rio
sources.citation_text: The Museu de Arte do Rio catalog identifies Cunhambebe (d. 1555) as the greatest leader during the Tamoio confederation and notes the possible father-son name duplication.
